source_caption:
Julia Roberts and Aaron Eckhart in Erin Brockovich (2000)

It’s a gripping true story about Erin, who, after a car accident that wasn’t her fault, pushes her lawyer Ed Masry to give her a job at his firm. While working there, she comes across some medical records hidden in real estate files and gets curious.

What starts as a small discovery turns into something much bigger as she uncovers a cover-up involving contaminated water that’s making people in a local community seriously sick. From there, Erin takes it on herself to dig deeper and fight for the people who’ve been affected.

source_details.title: Erin Brockovich
source_details.synopsis: Erin Brockovich is a 2000 American biographical legal drama film directed by Steven Soderbergh and written by Susannah Grant. The film is a dramatization of the true story of Erin Brockovich, portrayed by Julia Roberts, who initiated a legal case against the Pacific Gas and Electric Company over its culpability for the Hinkley groundwater contamination incident. Erin Brockovich premiered in Los Angeles on March 14, 2000, and was released theatrically in the United States by Universal Pictures on March 17, 2000, and internationally by Columbia TriStar Film Distributors International.
